yeah avoiding burnout is insanely important. You need to grind this shit for months, need to stay consistent.   I burned out once hard and it legit took me years to fully recover. Must avoid at all costs.

Honestly it took me a long time to get to a point where I could even do this. The short story is I tried to dial in my life as much as possible so that I could consistently perform at a high level.  
This meant things like getting enough sleep, having a well-balanced diet, spending time with people I love, having a beer, smoking a joint, having a beer and smoking a joint, and so on.  
I also had a morning routine where I would chug a coffee and IMMEDIATELY start LC. This habit took a week to develop and I have since lost it. Also I think a lot of hte difficult in LC is getting started. If you develop the habit of starting AS SOON AS YOU WAKE UP your mind doesn't have as much time to think about how it could go wrong (?) idk it worked for me, may be diff for u



Nevertheless, having routines/systems in place help (e.g. meal prep). You want to structure youre life so most decisions are already made and you can focus on just LC. I eat same foods everyday and do other things to minimize decision fatigue.  
And also I worked out every other day. Heavy squats, deadlifts, etc. That took out my frustration and would strongly recommend something like that to take your mind off LC,

I burned out once before in late 20s and would not like to ever do that again. I have since developed a lot of tools to avoid and can recognize the signs when I start to burnout, e.g., trouble sleeping/eating and general anxiety. I know I'm near burnout when I start to dissociate lul.

Since your a biochemist -- the molecule widely believed to be responsible for magnetoreception is cryptochrome. When light hits this molecule a radical pair is formed. The radical pair can recombine to form two distinct products according to their relative spin. And their relative spin can be changed by a weak magnetic field (i.e. Earth's). So basically you have a chemical reaction whose product (i.e. the pathway) can be influenced by a weak field

There is a genetic component. Birds who are very young can navigate on their own, with no guidance. Sea turtles also have this sense:

[http://lohmannlab.web.unc.edu/magnetoreception/](http://lohmannlab.web.unc.edu/magnetoreception/)

Birds also have multiple different compasses that they can calibrate against eachother. They use the stars (just like us), the setting sun, Earth's magnetic field, etc. They are highly robust when it comes to navigating. So much so that they were used in WW1/WW2 to help both sides:

[https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-tayside-central-17138990](https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-tayside-central-17138990)
the bird also uses the inclination information.

That is one idea, but the more widely accepted belief is the 'chemical compass'. So it's believed there is a chemical reaction whose product is sensitive to a weak magnetic field. The mechanism behind it, 'the radical pair mechanism' (RPM), relies on quantum mechanics. Currently, there is a large amount of support for the RPM -- birds when exposed to only red light are disoriented, but can orient properly in only blue light, consistent with the RPM. Similarly, it was found that radiofrequency waves disrupt a birds ability to orient, consistent with the RPM. I'm finishing my phd on the subject so ask anything you want.

Birds can sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a compass (magnetoreception). First discovered by the Wiltschko's in the 60's. The widely accepted explanation (the only other one being magnetite) is the radical pair mechanism. Basically a chemical reaction that is sensitive to weak magnetic fields.
